sections.title: The letter U
paragraphs: The letter name is (U) /uː/. Its main sound is a vowel heard in (Uhr) /uːɐ̯/, which means clock, watch. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. This letter makes two sounds in German.

sections.title: Mouth movements
paragraphs: For the first sound, pull your tongue back and push your lips forward into a small circle. Hold the sound. For the second sound, pull your tongue back, keep your mouth slightly wider, and make a short sound. A short sound is a sound that you say very quickly. Touch your throat to feel it shake.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: Before a single consonant or before the letter h, say the first sound, as in (gut) /ɡuːt/. Before two or more consonants, say the second sound, as in (und) /ʊnt/ or (Mutter) /ˈmʊtɐ/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not add a glide like the sound in boot. Keep your lips still from start to finish. For the short variant, do not say the open vowel in but. Shape your lips into a circle instead.
